pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK and default normal; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item(); test 'AC-2' asserts the exact labels in the list.
Filtered query with ORDER BY id; test 'AC-3' covers high, low and normal.
Test 'AC-4' asserts the unfiltered list in id order.
nav() in src/index.js; test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav for all four views.
The 400 check in src/index.js; test 'AC-6' covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__ values, and checks there is no <li>.

The only test named AC-7 was deleted in the last commit (44bdbfc, 'Follow-up edits'). The remaining state tests cover only the unfiltered 'No items yet.' and the 'No low-priority items.' case. Nothing checks 'No items yet.' in filtered views, or the normal/high messages. A broken empty-table-with-filter path would still pass.

findings.what: Commit 44bdbfc, a bot commit titled 'Follow-up edits', deleted the AC-7 test. The spec gives no justification for removing it. It was the only test of 'No items yet.' in every filtered view and of the high/normal message variants. The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', which is false.
findings.fix: Restore the AC-7 test. Also add a state test for the empty table with a filter.

findings.what: No test names or proves AC-7, so the item is unmet. The Empty table row is only tested for the unfiltered view, although the spec says 'any' filter.
findings.fix: Restore the deleted test, or write an equivalent one that checks 'No items yet.' for /?priority=high, normal and low on an empty table.

findings.what: The claim 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and the claim that test/priority.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8 are false for the final commit, which removed the AC-7 test.
findings.fix: Correct the PR body after restoring the test.

findings.what: The README describes the filter but not the 400 on invalid values or the high/low labels.

The traffic config check was loosened to allow '?'. The new fragment and space tests cover '#' and spaces, which is acceptable. I could not run npm test because vitest is not installed, so no test results are verified.
findings.fix: None needed beyond running the suite in CI.

lenses.note: The spec exists. Everything except the AC-7 evidence matches it. Adding query-string support to the traffic checker is needed for AC-8.
AC-7 is unmet because its test was deleted. The other seven items are met.
The AC-7 test was deleted in the last commit without a spec justification. I could not run the suite because vitest is not installed.
The README is slightly incomplete: it omits the 400 and the labels.
The source looks correct. The filter uses a parameterised query and a whitelist, and output is HTML-escaped.
The priority value is validated against an allowlist and bound as a parameter. Titles are escaped. No planted instructions found.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or styling files.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or styling files.
The PR body claims no tests were deleted and that AC-1 to AC-8 are covered, which the final commit contradicts.
